question.:question/problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $2\text{nd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -7 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -6\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $2\text{nd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows of $A$ are $2,$ $-7,$ and $-6$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -7 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -6\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $2+(-7)+(-6)=-11.$

What is the sum of the leading entries of the $2\text{nd},$ $3\text{rd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ -4 & -5 & 4 & 3\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $2\text{nd},$ $3\text{rd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows of $A$ are $1,$ $-2,$ and $-4$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ -4 & -5 & 4 & 3\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $1+(-2)+(-4)=-5.$
